hook: A derandomized low-degree test can fail with about q^(3/2) lines, yet works once the field is larger
hook_turn: yet works once the field is larger
summary: A low-degree test checks whether a function is close to a polynomial by looking at random lines. The authors build a function and a set of nearly q^(3/2) lines where agreement is about 1/2 on each line, yet the function is far from low-degree polynomials. They also prove the test works with O(q) lines when the field is large enough. The results cover the two-variable case only.
title: On derandomizing the line-point low-degree test
